kf: The most common imported arboviral infection in the UK (UKHSA: 904 cases in 2024).
Fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia; then a rash with **"white islands in a sea of red"** during recovery.
**Critical phase days 3–7**: warning signs (abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding, lethargy, rising haematocrit with falling platelets).
Supportive care: **paracetamol only**; avoid aspirin, ibuprofen and NSAIDs (bleeding risk).
Any fever in a returning traveller → same-day medical assessment.
myths: **"Dengue is always mild"**: second infection with a different serotype raises the risk of severe dengue.
patho_lead: Severe dengue is due to **leaky capillaries**, often worse on a second infection.

mech.t: Aedes mosquitoes transmit the virus, mainly by day.
Virus infects immune cells, causing fever and pain.
Non-neutralising antibodies from a past serotype can increase viral uptake.
Cytokines and endothelial damage cause leakage around defervescence.
A confluent rash with spared islands appears.
mech.cap: White islands in a sea of red.

prog: Case fatality in severe dengue under 1% with good supportive care.
